# Analysis freeze v1.0 (pre-annotation)

**Frozen:** 2026-09-29, from committed results at `a08828d` (`research/improvement`).
**Generated by:** `research/experiments/freeze_analysis_report.js`. Do not edit by hand: change an analysis, rerun it, then regenerate this file.
**Status:** this is the analysis used by the EACL 2027 SRW mentorship draft.
**Supersession:** v2.0 replaces it after the two-annotator study and the v0.2.1 re-run (T11–T12). Every number below comes from the result files listed in §12.

**Conventions used throughout:**

- **Brackets** are 95% intervals: percentile bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 42) unless marked Wilson or Clopper–Pearson.
- **Evaluation protocol:** 5-fold cross-validation stratified by label, seed 42. Every tuned quantity (α, thresholds, calibrators) is chosen on the 4 development folds and applied once to the test fold.
- **Status:** all analyses are exploratory, specified after results were seen.

## 1. Populations and denominators

| Population | v0.1 | v0.2 | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| All queries | 150 | 209 | appendix figures, bare-keyword and Split B checks (controls included) |
| Canonical controls (verbatim corpus intents, always answered correctly) | 25 | 25 | excluded from headline figures |
| Non-control queries | 125 | 184 | calibration, ranking, Tables 1–3, Figure 1 |
| — of which in-scope (non-OOD) | 110 | 134 | accuracy, false rejections |
| — of which out-of-scope (OOD) | 15 | 50 | out-of-scope rejection |
| Answerable queries (shared by both versions) | 121 | 121 | sensitivity only |
| OOD: original v0.1 items / items added in v0.2 | 15 / 0 | 15 / 35 | screening check |

- **Versions.** v0.2 contains all of v0.1, so the two are not independent samples.
- **Reproduction.** The published baseline reproduces exactly (0/150 mismatches). Mean latency 3.29 ms in the archived run (3.2129 ms in the reproduction run), on one machine; indicative only.

## 2. Confidence and calibration (non-control queries)

**Setup.**

- Isotonic recalibration is fit on development folds; controls are excluded from both fit and evaluation.
- The noise floor is the ECE of a perfectly calibrated forecaster with the same confidences and n (2,000 simulations, seed 7).
- Brier skill is measured against an out-of-fold forecaster that predicts the development base rate.

| Confidence | Ver. | n | ECE raw | ECE isotonic | Reduction | Equal-mass / sweep ECE (isotonic) | Noise floor mean / p95 | Brier skill raw | Brier skill isotonic |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shipped | v0.1 | 125 | 0.323 | 0.069 | 79% [44%, 84%] | 0.110 / 0.059 | 0.064 / 0.105 | -0.227 [-0.453, 0.012] | 0.205 [0.040, 0.359] |
| Hybrid (fused top-1) | v0.1 | 125 | 0.329 | 0.108 | 67% [43%, 83%] | 0.108 / 0.055 | 0.054 / 0.089 | -0.321 [-0.500, -0.105] | 0.380 [0.204, 0.542] |
| Shipped | v0.2 | 184 | 0.293 | 0.063 | 78% [52%, 87%] | 0.070 / 0.047 | 0.050 / 0.080 | -0.058 [-0.258, 0.145] | 0.327 [0.185, 0.460] |
| Hybrid (fused top-1) | v0.2 | 184 | 0.368 | 0.071 | 81% [62%, 86%] | 0.058 / 0.071 | 0.051 / 0.079 | -0.304 [-0.500, -0.100] | 0.405 [0.269, 0.534] |

**Calibrator comparison** (shipped confidence, ECE / Brier; differences between calibrators not tested):

| Ver. | none | isotonic | Platt | histogram binning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v0.1 | 0.323 / 0.305 | 0.069 / 0.198 | 0.087 / 0.201 | 0.101 / 0.201 |
| v0.2 | 0.293 / 0.266 | 0.063 / 0.169 | 0.045 / 0.166 | 0.039 / 0.174 |

- Histogram binning is scored on the bins it fits, and has the worst Brier score of the three calibrators in every case.
- Recalibration changes the confidence shown, not the answer.
- Shipped correctness AUROC falls from 0.742 to 0.686 (v0.1), because each fold has its own map.

## 3. Selective prediction and ranking (non-control queries, tie-aware)

**Method.** Risk-coverage curves use the exact expected risk under a random order within tied confidences, not benchmark row order. OOD answers count as errors.

| Ver. | System | n | Errors | Largest tie block | Risk at 50% coverage (range over tie orders) | AURC | AUGRC | Correctness AUROC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v0.1 | Shipped | 125 | 53 | 85 (68%) at conf 1, 22 errors | 25.9% (0.0%–34.9%) | 0.286 [0.200, 0.380] | 0.153 [0.110, 0.200] | 0.742 [0.662, 0.817] |
| v0.1 | Hybrid | 125 | 46 | 71 (57%) at conf 1, 8 errors | 11.3% (0.0%–12.7%) | 0.171 [0.105, 0.247] | 0.105 [0.069, 0.145] | 0.841 [0.765, 0.908] |
| v0.2 | Shipped | 184 | 89 | 103 (56%) at conf 1, 23 errors | 22.3% (13.0%–25.0%) | 0.283 [0.211, 0.363] | 0.162 [0.125, 0.202] | 0.819 [0.761, 0.874] |
| v0.2 | Hybrid | 184 | 83 | 85 (46%) at conf 1, 10 errors | 14.1% (14.1%–14.1%) | 0.208 [0.146, 0.278] | 0.132 [0.098, 0.170] | 0.877 [0.826, 0.923] |

**Paired differences, hybrid minus shipped** (paired bootstrap):

| Ver. | AURC | AUGRC | Correctness AUROC |
|---|---|---|---|
| v0.1 | -0.115 [-0.177, -0.054] | -0.048 [-0.073, -0.024] | 0.099 [0.008, 0.190] |
| v0.2 | -0.075 [-0.126, -0.024] | -0.030 [-0.050, -0.011] | 0.058 [-0.001, 0.118] |

AURC and AUGRC mix ranking with accuracy. Correctness AUROC isolates ranking; its v0.2 interval includes zero.

## 4. Accuracy (non-control in-scope queries)

| System | v0.1 | v0.2 |
|---|---|---|
| BM25 (shipped) | 72/110 (65.5%) | 95/134 (70.9%) |
| Dense (MiniLM) | 73/110 (66.4%) | 90/134 (67.2%) |
| Hybrid | 79/110 (71.8%) | 101/134 (75.4%) |

| Ver. | Comparison | Discordant (other only – hybrid only) | Gain, pp | Exact McNemar p | Mid-p | Asymptotic p |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v0.1 | hybrid vs BM25 | 0–7 | 6.36 [1.82, 10.91] | 0.0156 | 0.0078 | 0.0082 |
| v0.1 | hybrid vs dense | 3–9 | 5.45 [0.00, 11.82] | 0.1460 | 0.0923 | 0.0833 |
| v0.2 | hybrid vs BM25 | 1–7 | 4.48 [0.75, 8.96] | 0.0703 | 0.0391 | 0.0339 |
| v0.2 | hybrid vs dense | 3–14 | 8.21 [2.24, 14.18] | 0.0127 | 0.0075 | 0.0076 |

- **Ties with the tests.** Controls are never discordant, so the p values are identical with the controls included.
- **Bootstrap vs exact test.** The bootstrap intervals are not dual to the exact test.
- **Rounding.** Intervals are shown at the 2 decimals stored in `phase1_t1`. The v0.2 lower bound 0.75 is the bootstrap quantile 1/134 = 0.746 pp, which the paper shows as 0.7.
- **v0.2 hybrid vs BM25** is the only comparison whose side of 0.05 depends on the test used.

## 6. Out-of-scope rejection

**The three rules:**

- **Fixed:** the shipped rule, raw BM25 < 2.0.
- **Tuned threshold:** raw BM25 below an F1-maximizing threshold, chosen per fold on development folds.
- **Detector:** the hybrid fused top-1 score, thresholded the same way.

False rejections are counted over non-control in-scope queries; no rule ever rejects a control.

| Ver. | Rule | OOD rejected (Wilson) | False rejections | Thresholds per fold |

| v0.1 | Fixed rule | 4/15 (26.7%; 10.9%–51.9%) | 0/110 | 2.0 |

## 8. Risky answers and the risk classifier (no safety claim)

**Setup.**

- Risk tiers come from a deterministic rule-based classifier applied to each returned command.
- The classifier misses at least one destructive command, so risky counts are lower bounds.
- Population: non-control queries, with OOD included.

| Ver. | System | Answered | High/critical returned | Of which wrong | Wrong at max confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v0.1 | Shipped | 121 | 20 | 2 | 1 |
| v0.1 | Hybrid | 125 | 23 | 3 | 1 |
| v0.2 | Shipped | 167 | 21 | 2 | 1 |
| v0.2 | Hybrid | 184 | 26 | 6 | 1 |

**Wrong and risky answers.** No control is among them. Confidence is on each system's own scale: the shipped tool in %, the hybrid as a fused score in [0, 1].

## 10. Label reliability

- **κ.** A partially independent reviewer re-labelled 14 AI-authored v0.2 queries: Cohen's κ = 0.6316. The percentile bootstrap 95% interval is [0.391, 1.000] (9993/10000 valid resamples). This is below the pre-specified 0.7 target.
- **OOD labels.** The reviewer agreed on 8/8 (Clopper–Pearson [63%, 100%]). Of these, 7 were everyday requests and 1 a far-from-corpus task; none was a terminal task.
- **Disagreements.** All three were on ambiguous labels (3 of 6).
- **Pending.** The two-annotator study of all 59 AI-authored queries is under way. Its results will go into v2.0 of this report.

## 11. Limitations the manuscript must carry

- Small, dependent, partly AI-authored benchmark (150 and 209 queries; 59 drafted by an AI agent); label check below target; the annotation study has no results yet.
- All analyses were specified after the results were seen: the Holm family, the controls exclusion, the equal-false-rejection comparison and the sensitivity subsets. Accuracy tests rest on 7–8 discordant queries.
- Headline numbers use one fold partition (seed 42). Twenty partitions support the ranking and out-of-scope results, but "within the noise floor" is partition-dependent.
- Only 10 OOD queries are terminal tasks. Kind labels are AI-assigned. The added OOD queries were screened with raw retrieval scores, which favors the shipped score. The detector features were chosen on the full data, which may flatter the detector.
- Scope: one tool, one platform (Windows corpus of 279 commands), one small encoder (all-MiniLM-L6-v2), one fusion rule, exact-match scoring, and single-machine latency. No generative system, user study or public benchmark.
- The risk classifier is scored against the benchmark's own labels, two of which are inconsistent. It misses at least one destructive command. The functional check covers 15 queries and treats exit code 0 as success.
- Ground-truth defects: TA-B145 and TA-B187 (v0.2 only) have gold commands outside the corpus; TA-B149 has an acceptable command outside it. They lower non-OOD accuracy by 1 (v0.1) and 2 (v0.2) queries for every system.
